# Lab 12.10: Time-Series Forecasting: ARIMA_PLUS

## What We Are Going to Do
Forecast daily bike trips for several stations at once with ARIMA_PLUS, including holidays, then add an external regressor with ARIMA_PLUS_XREG.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Build daily series per station.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE lab12.daily_trips AS
SELECT DATE(start_time) AS day, start_station_name AS station, COUNT(*) AS trips
FROM `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips`
WHERE start_station_name IN (
  SELECT start_station_name FROM `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips`
  GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 5)
GROUP BY day, station;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[SQL] Train one model for all 5 series.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL lab12.trips_arima
OPTIONS (
  model_type = 'ARIMA_PLUS',
  time_series_timestamp_col = 'day',
  time_series_data_col = 'trips',
  time_series_id_col = 'station',
  holiday_region = 'US',
  horizon = 30
) AS SELECT * FROM lab12.daily_trips;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[SQL] Forecast and explain.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT station, forecast_timestamp, ROUND(forecast_value) AS forecast,
       ROUND(prediction_interval_lower_bound) AS low, ROUND(prediction_interval_upper_bound) AS high
FROM ML.FORECAST(MODEL lab12.trips_arima, STRUCT(14 AS horizon, 0.9 AS confidence_level))
ORDER BY station, forecast_timestamp;

SELECT * FROM ML.EXPLAIN_FORECAST(MODEL lab12.trips_arima, STRUCT(14 AS horizon)) LIMIT 20;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[Console] Chart it.** Run the first query in step 3. In the results pane open **Chart**, x-axis `forecast_timestamp`, y-axis `forecast`, series `station`.

5. **[SQL] Add an external regressor.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL lab12.trips_xreg
OPTIONS (model_type = 'ARIMA_PLUS_XREG', time_series_timestamp_col = 'day', time_series_data_col = 'trips', horizon = 14)
AS
SELECT day, trips, IF(EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM day) IN (1, 7), 1, 0) AS is_weekend
FROM lab12.daily_trips WHERE station = (SELECT ANY_VALUE(station) FROM lab12.daily_trips);

SELECT * FROM ML.FORECAST(MODEL lab12.trips_xreg, STRUCT(14 AS horizon),
  (SELECT d AS day, IF(EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM d) IN (1, 7), 1, 0) AS is_weekend
   FROM UNNEST(GENERATE_DATE_ARRAY(
     (SELECT MAX(day) + 1 FROM lab12.daily_trips), (SELECT MAX(day) + 14 FROM lab12.daily_trips))) d));</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


6. **[CLI] Save the forecast to a table with bq.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq query --use_legacy_sql=false --destination_table=lab12.trips_forecast --replace \
'SELECT * FROM ML.FORECAST(MODEL lab12.trips_arima, STRUCT(30 AS horizon))'
bq head -n 5 lab12.trips_forecast</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| One model | 5 station series |
| Holidays | US holidays modelled |
| `ML.EXPLAIN_FORECAST` | Trend, seasonality and holiday parts |
| XREG | Uses known future values (weekend flag) |
